currentContext.strengths: Scale leadership in print: 'India's largest print media company', publishing 5 newspapers across 61 editions and 211 sub-editions in 14 states and 3 languages|Largest printing infrastructure in the industry - 51 printing facilities, stated as the highest in the Indian newspaper industry|Reach moat: readership of 6.63 crore (IRS 2019 Q4) covering markets representing 49% of India's urban population and 58% of India's land area (Census 2011)|Digital leadership in Indian languages: Dainik Bhaskar and Divya Bhaskar news apps remain the #1 Hindi and Gujarati news apps, with MAUs around 20 million as of March 2026 (Dainik Bhaskar app up from ~1.6 million monthly users in 2020 to 16.8 million as of March 2026)|Editorial/newsroom depth: ~12,000 journalists across print and digital, enabling hyperlocal ground reporting; recognised with two Ramnath Goenka Awards for Excellence in Journalism 2026|Brand trust and hyperlocal 'ground connect' built over decades, cited as the basis for advertiser confidence and reader stickiness|Debt-free balance sheet with strong cash generation, providing resilience and flexibility to invest in growth|Diversified media portfolio across print, digital and radio, allowing the group to serve audiences across multiple consumer touchpoints ('phygital' presence)|Circulation resilience - circulation business remained stable and the Company states it continued to gain market share in several markets, against an industry where circulation revenues declined ~1% in 2025
currentContext.strategies: Digital is positioned as a key focus area and an important pillar of the Company's long-term growth strategy, built on sustained investment in high-quality content, superior user experience, technology capabilities and talent to grow a highly engaged, loyal user base.|Strengthen an integrated "phygital" presence across print and digital through investments in digital capabilities, technology platforms and high-quality content offerings.|Editorial excellence, hyperlocal relevance and meaningful audience engagement are stated as the core of the Company's growth strategy, used to deepen the connect with readers and advertisers and reinforce leadership position across markets.|Disciplined cost management and operational efficiencies to hold stable operating performance and healthy margins despite volatility in newsprint prices, higher raw material costs and foreign exchange movements.|Continued emphasis on circulation growth, reader engagement initiatives and strengthening market position across core markets.|Use demographic insights, user preferences, location, economic segment and real-time context to predict and serve content, targeting engagement, long-term retention, loyalty and willingness to pay; leverage technology to scale journalism across formats from original/exclusive stories to real-time hyperlocal content.|Expand the MY FM radio network using the Private FM Radio Phase III licences won, prioritising smaller markets where MY FM becomes the first and only private radio broadcaster (Daman, Gandhidham, Bhuj, Ratlam, Pali, Sri Ganganagar, Alwar).|One editorial philosophy across every newsroom in the network — truth, public interest and reader trust — while responding to the unique local priorities of each region (Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Punjab, Chandigarh).|Combine editorial creativity with technology — QR-enabled print-to-digital experiences, drone visuals, infographics and audio series — to move readers between print and digital platforms.|Solar Power Plants installed at various plants and offices of the Company having capacity of 3,545 KW peak (BRSR resource-efficiency initiative — stated as installed capacity achieved, NOT a dated forward target)
currentContext.expansion: DBCL is an asset-light-to-moderate print media business whose expansion narrative in FY 2025-26 is about printing infrastructure and renewable-energy build-out rather than greenfield capacity projects. The Company states it operates a state-of-the-art printing infrastructure spread across 12 states, featuring 78 advanced machines, with an impressive installed capacity of around 3.2 million copies per hour, which it says enables it to produce and distribute high-quality newspapers efficiently. It describes significant investments in advanced technology, incorporating state-of-the-art CTPs and high-speed presses from globally recognised brands, alongside a range of innovative printing solutions for advertisers and readers (3D printing, fragrance printing, fuzzy folds, butterfly flaps, French windows, super panorama, UV printing, Front Page Cloth printing, Front Page Mica Paper printing and Feel & Reveal). The only quantified expansion programme described in the narrative chapters is solar: the Board's Report states that an investment of ` 22.96 million was made during FY 2025-26 for installation / capacity enhancement of Solar PV plants, split between new installations at Indore, Nashik, Akola, Nagaur and Kota Office (545 kWp) and capacity enhancements at Jaipur, Kota, Ajmer, Sikar and Bharatpur (330 kWp). In FY 2025-26 a total solar PV plant capacity of 875 kWp was added, taking total solar installed capacity across locations to 3,545 kWp; total solar generation was 37,25,811 kWh and total saving of ` 27.33 million was achieved through solar generation. Other energy work described is efficiency rather than capacity: individual monitoring of every location's electrical panel power factor, conversion of press drive systems from analog to digital drives for accurate speed control and steady production, and replacement of conventional lights with LED. The BRSR states that 1.52% of capex investments in FY 2025-26 went into specific technologies to improve environmental and social impacts (Nil in FY 2024-25), attributed to solar. No new print centre, edition launch, acquisition, JV, radio-station rollout or plant commissioning timeline is disclosed anywhere in the routed text, and the MD&A extract supplied is industry/economy commentary (Indian economy, M&E sector, print advertising and events) rather than a company expansion plan.
currentContext.mdna: Print remained resilient in India despite global declines; the print segment was largely stable in 2025 and is estimated at ₹ 259 billion, with advertising revenues up 2% and circulation revenues down 1%.|Print remains the preferred medium for reaching affluent, decision-making audiences and the platform of choice for premium sectors such as automotive, real estate, education, BFSI and retail, particularly for product launches and high-impact campaigns.|Print advertising revenues are projected to grow at a CAGR of approximately 2%, supported by the medium's continued effectiveness in reaching affluent consumers and promoting premium, high-value products.|Advertising is expected to grow by over 3% in 2026 and at a CAGR of 2% until 2028, driven by advertisers' ability to reach increasingly elusive affluent audiences who can skip digital advertisements, and by premium inventory formats that sustain revenues even as circulation continues to decline.|Ad insertion volumes rose 2% over 2024 — a third consecutive year of growth — while ad rates remained largely flat; advertiser count on print rose to almost 150,000 across 669 categories and 179,000 brands, with Hindi the largest contributor at 37% of total newspaper ad volumes.|Government advertising rates increased by 26% towards the end of 2025, a pricing reset EY estimates will translate into an additional 2% to 3% increase in overall advertising revenues provided volumes are sustained, with the impact more pronounced for regional and smaller publishers where government advertising is a baseline revenue stream.|Events are emerging as a high-growth area, expected to contribute approximately 4% to 6% of the segment's total advertising revenues by 2027; print is also evolving into a performance medium, with one in every three print advertisements carrying a call to action (QR code, time-bound offer, e-commerce/q-commerce incentive or contest).|Publishers are shifting from traffic-led models to trust-based, loyalty-driven ecosystems supported by subscriptions, memberships, communities and branded content.|As AI-generated summaries reduce referral traffic by 30%, credibility is expected to become the key differentiator for publishers, and a governance-first approach to AI adoption is expected to emerge as a competitive advantage; the reach of online news platforms fell 9% in 2025 with AI search summaries cited as a key reason.|The News in Education (NIE) programme is expected to see renewed focus, with potential state-government mandates to incorporate news into school and college curricula raising circulation to educational institutions and building long-term readership habits.|The M&E sector grew 9% in 2025 to ₹ 2.78 trillion (US$32 billion) and is expected to grow 2.8% in 2026 to ₹ 2.86 trillion (US$32.9 billion); excluding online gaming it is expected to grow 8% in 2026 and thereafter at a CAGR of over 7%, reaching ₹ 3.3 trillion (US$37.9 billion) by 2028.|The digital media segment crossed ₹ 1 trillion and is expected to grow at a CAGR of 14% to ₹ 1,640 billion by 2028; digital advertising grew 26% to ₹ 947 billion in 2025 as FMCG, travel and pharma shifted spends from traditional media.|News subscriptions are expected to grow at 20% but remain sub-scale at just ₹ 8 billion by 2028, with innovation around value-accretive products and high-value communities the route to growth in niche segments.|Regional content is the growth vector — 56% of content produced for digital platforms in 2025 was in regional languages, and with urban tele-density at 136% versus 59% rural, the next wave of content consumption growth is expected to come from Bharat rather than urban India.|Radio ad volumes rose marginally by 2% in 2025 but fell by up to 20% in high-yield metro markets while yields fell 9% on average; non-FCT revenues were 25% of radio segment revenues and are expected to contribute around 39% of total revenues by 2028, requiring the industry to redefine its value proposition.|Consumption is expected to drive the next wave of economic expansion, with PFCE at 57% of GDP in fiscal 2026, policy tailwinds from the 8th Pay Commission and GST rate rationalisation, nuclear families, rising female workforce participation, and GDP per capita rising from $3.0k to more than $4.5k; Crisil projects India's real GDP growth at 7.1% and corporate revenue growth at 8-9% in fiscal 2027.|Company-level: the Print business maintained strong momentum led by improved overall advertiser sentiment, with advertising demand strong across education, real estate, healthcare, automobile and government, supported by improving consumption trends.|Company-level: newsprint prices rose on supply disruptions from global geopolitical tensions, higher raw material costs and foreign exchange movements, which the Company anticipates is a temporary disruption for a couple of upcoming months.|Company-level: management remains optimistic about opportunities across print, digital and radio, supported by improving consumption trends and growing aspirations across Tier II and Tier III markets.|Company-level: Radio segment revenues declined 7% industry-wide in 2025 while the Company's Radio business revenue decline was 5%.

risks.risk: Macroeconomic and geopolitical risk feeding through to advertising spend
risks.note: Management flags that global geopolitical tensions, trade disruptions, inflationary pressures and commodity-market volatility could hit economic activity and business sentiment, and that any slowdown in economic growth may result in lower advertising expenditure across sectors, thereby affecting industry revenues. Advertising is the company's primary revenue engine, so this is a direct earnings transmission channel rather than a generic macro caveat.

risks.risk: Input cost volatility — imported newsprint and foreign exchange exposure
risks.note: The newspaper industry remains exposed to fluctuations in newsprint prices, foreign exchange movements and other input costs. Since a significant portion of newsprint requirements is met through imports, adverse movements in global commodity prices or currency exchange rates could impact profitability. The BRSR sourcing disclosure corroborates the structural import dependence: 73.00% of total newsprint was procured from local and national suppliers within India in FY 2025-26 (67.00% in FY 2024-25), leaving the balance sourced internationally.

risks.risk: Technology and platform disruption, including AI-driven content aggregation
risks.note: Rapid technological advancements, changing consumer preferences and increasing dependence on global technology platforms can alter content discovery and consumption patterns. Management specifically flags that the emergence of artificial-intelligence-driven content aggregation and search mechanisms may impact traffic flows and monetisation opportunities for publishers — a structural threat to the digital growth engine the company is investing behind.

risks.risk: Content piracy and weak intellectual property enforcement
risks.note: The digital media industry continues to face content piracy and unauthorized distribution of content. Weak enforcement of intellectual property rights and rapid proliferation of digital platforms are named as key concerns that can adversely affect monetisation and investments in original content — i.e. it undermines the return on the company's stated heavy spend on original and exclusive content.

risks.risk: External and unforeseen events (pandemics, natural disasters, geopolitical conflict)
risks.note: Management states that such events may adversely affect economic activity, consumer sentiment and advertising expenditure, and explicitly concedes that while the Company continuously monitors developments and maintains appropriate preparedness measures, the impact of such events remains inherently uncertain — an acknowledged unhedgeable tail risk for an ad-funded business.

risks.risk: Cyber-security, data privacy and IT/business-continuity dependence
risks.note: Business continuity is anchored on a single critical system: the SAP system is backed up daily and synced continuously with a Disaster Recovery Server, with a disaster recovery site for SAP at a Mumbai data centre. The company relies on an information security management policy (data protection; email, web and network protection; access control with two-factor authentication; firewall and end-point protection) to prevent data attacks and threats. Disclosed outcome for FY 2025-26: nil data breaches and nil cyber-security consumer complaints.

one-line thesis: Print advertising is doing what most media formats aren't — Q1 ad revenue +10% YoY broad-based across categories (ex-education/auto), driving 250 bps EBITDA-margin expansion to 26.1% and +25% PAT, even as newsprint cost inflated ~13% YoY. The structural story is unchanged: circulation copies keep drifting down (~38 lakh vs ~40 lakh two years ago) with flat realization, so the equity case rests on ad-yield/market-share gains and cost discipline offsetting a slowly shrinking reader base; digital (~20m MAU) remains a long-dated, still-immaterial option.

> Ad growth is "a little bit of both" pricing + volume, "more of volume." Education (Q1's largest ad category, ~20%) was flat because NEET was re-examined in June, shifting result-season advertising into Q2; automobile fell to single-digit on geopolitical/fuel issues. Other operating-income jump = higher job-work & wastage revenue (per CFO).
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Revenue growth:** no formal guidance ("I can't give any guidance… everybody is working hard"). Ad momentum broad-based; education expected to recover in Q2 (NEET shift), so H1 education growth "good."
- **Margin:** no explicit target; drivers = cost saving + top-line, company-wide cost discipline (non-newsprint costs).
- **Newsprint (cost):** +13% YoY / +8% QoQ in Q1 to ~INR 53,000/tonne; expected to **rise further in Q2**, then **start coming down in Q3 and Q4 FY27**.
- **Capex FY27:** ~INR 150–160 crore ("around the same range"), largely buying/building owned property to replace high rentals (e.g. Bhopal).
- **Radio:** 7 more stations lined up (on 37); good bottom-line growth targeted via cost control; ~12% growth described as ambitious/"humongous task."
- Segment-leadership/circulation-promotion spend ~INR 20–25 crore annually.
order book & pipeline: N/A — media/advertising business, no order book. Forward ad visibility tied to festive/election cycle: **Uttar Pradesh state election ~March next year** flagged as a big ad opportunity (and digital focus market, no print presence there).
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Print + Digital:** EBITDA INR 1,499 mn (+18%). 250 district editions, ~1,700 news pages/day, ~14,000 stories + 1,800 videos/day across print+digital reporters.
- **Circulation:** ~38 lakh copies (39 lakh Q4, ~40 lakh Q3, 43–44 lakh two years ago). Realization flat; deliberate choice not to hike cover price while ad grows. Market-share gains cited in Rajasthan & MP.
- **Radio (My FM):** 37 stations, +7 planned; revenue INR 425 mn, EBITDA INR 148 mn (+29%), ad +12%; space/time inventory fixed so growth via innovation.
- **Digital:** ~19–20 million MAU (May 2026); #1 Hindi & Gujarati news app; revenue "miniscule," <5% of total, mostly advertising, growing off a small base; monetization is a long-term call, focus still on reader-base build (UP a key market).
growth verticals / optionality:
- Digital news apps + AI-generated micro-dramas ("Bhaskar series" based on news, not fiction) — early traction, cross-posted to YouTube; English app later (resources in Hindi/Gujarati).
- UP digital-first expansion ahead of state elections; radio station additions.
margins & cost dynamics: - 250 bps margin expansion despite newsprint inflation, via decentralized cost control (travel, admin pushed to all team members, not just HO). Newsprint is the single largest cost and outside management control; everything else is the lever.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): - FY27 capex ~INR 150–160 crore, continuing the FY26 step-up. Rationale: convert high-rental locations to owned buildings (Bhopal bought & building own premises + a couple more stations) to save rent and capture property appreciation.
capital allocation: - Capex skewed to owned real estate (rent substitution); FDs on balance sheet generate interest (in other operating income). No buyback/dividend commentary this call. Card notes promoter-stake-consolidation theme (not discussed this call).
risks & watch-items:
- **Structural circulation decline** — copies down ~2–4%/yr as marginal readers move to digital; management admits "maybe a couple of percentages" market shrinkage.
- **Newsprint inflation** — Q2 to rise further before easing H2; margin hostage to it.
- **Ad cyclicality** — auto weak on macro; education timing-dependent (NEET); reliance on government (DAVP +26% price hike now flowing through).
- **Digital monetization** — years away from being 10–20% of revenue.
management quality / tone: - Confident, candid, numbers-fluent (Girish handled almost all Q&A). Honest about circulation drift ("we lose some copy, we gain some copy… teams go through frustration") and refusal to give guidance. Deliberately guarded on digital team size (competitive confidentiality).
non-obvious takeaways:
- Print ad growth is an outlier vs broadcasters' soft 1Q — supports the "print resilient in leadership Hindi/Gujarati markets" thesis.
- DAVP (government) +26% rate hike is a quiet tailwind driving double-digit government ad growth.
- Cover price frozen by choice (INR 4.93) — ad growth lets them subsidize readers to defend copies/market share; realization lever intentionally unused.
- Newsprint QoQ (+8%) already at ~INR 53,000; Q2 pain, then H2 relief is the key margin swing factor to verify.

| Advertising revenue | INR 4,320 mn | +~10% (vs INR 3,933 mn) | volume-led, pricing minor |
| Circulation revenue | INR 1,204 mn | ~flat/stable | copies ~38 lakh; cover price INR 4.93 (vs 4.9) |
| Print & other (print+digital) EBITDA | INR 1,499 mn | +18% (vs INR 1,270 mn) | excludes circulation-only & radio |
| Radio revenue / EBITDA | INR 425 mn / INR 148 mn | rev vs INR 392 mn ; EBITDA +29% (vs INR 115 mn) | 37 stations; ad +12% |
> Ad growth is "a little bit of both" pricing + volume, "more of volume." Education (Q1's largest ad category, ~20%) was flat because NEET was re-examined in June, shifting result-season advertising into Q2; automobile fell to single-digit on geopolitical/fuel issues. Other operating-income jump = higher job-work & wastage revenue (per CFO).
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Revenue growth:** no formal guidance ("I can't give any guidance… everybody is working hard"). Ad momentum broad-based; education expected to recover in Q2 (NEET shift), so H1 education growth "good."
- **Margin:** no explicit target; drivers = cost saving + top-line, company-wide cost discipline (non-newsprint costs).
- **Newsprint (cost):** +13% YoY / +8% QoQ in Q1 to ~INR 53,000/tonne; expected to **rise further in Q2**, then **start coming down in Q3 and Q4 FY27**.
- **Capex FY27:** ~INR 150–160 crore ("around the same range"), largely buying/building owned property to replace high rentals (e.g. Bhopal).
- **Radio:** 7 more stations lined up (on 37); good bottom-line growth targeted via cost control; ~12% growth described as ambitious/"humongous task."
- Segment-leadership/circulation-promotion spend ~INR 20–25 crore annually.
order book & pipeline: N/A — media/advertising business, no order book. Forward ad visibility tied to festive/election cycle: **Uttar Pradesh state election ~March next year** flagged as a big ad opportunity (and digital focus market, no print presence there).
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Print + Digital:** EBITDA INR 1,499 mn (+18%). 250 district editions, ~1,700 news pages/day, ~14,000 stories + 1,800 videos/day across print+digital reporters.
- **Circulation:** ~38 lakh copies (39 lakh Q4, ~40 lakh Q3, 43–44 lakh two years ago). Realization flat; deliberate choice not to hike cover price while ad grows. Market-share gains cited in Rajasthan & MP.
- **Radio (My FM):** 37 stations, +7 planned; revenue INR 425 mn, EBITDA INR 148 mn (+29%), ad +12%; space/time inventory fixed so growth via innovation.
- **Digital:** ~19–20 million MAU (May 2026); #1 Hindi & Gujarati news app; revenue "miniscule," <5% of total, mostly advertising, growing off a small base; monetization is a long-term call, focus still on reader-base build (UP a key market).
growth verticals / optionality:
- Digital news apps + AI-generated micro-dramas ("Bhaskar series" based on news, not fiction) — early traction, cross-posted to YouTube; English app later (resources in Hindi/Gujarati).
- UP digital-first expansion ahead of state elections; radio station additions.
margins & cost dynamics: - 250 bps margin expansion despite newsprint inflation, via decentralized cost control (travel, admin pushed to all team members, not just HO). Newsprint is the single largest cost and outside management control; everything else is the lever.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): - FY27 capex ~INR 150–160 crore, continuing the FY26 step-up. Rationale: convert high-rental locations to owned buildings (Bhopal bought & building own premises + a couple more stations) to save rent and capture property appreciation.
capital allocation: - Capex skewed to owned real estate (rent substitution); FDs on balance sheet generate interest (in other operating income). No buyback/dividend commentary this call. Card notes promoter-stake-consolidation theme (not discussed this call).
risks & watch-items:
- **Structural circulation decline** — copies down ~2–4%/yr as marginal readers move to digital; management admits "maybe a couple of percentages" market shrinkage.
- **Newsprint inflation** — Q2 to rise further before easing H2; margin hostage to it.
- **Ad cyclicality** — auto weak on macro; education timing-dependent (NEET); reliance on government (DAVP +26% price hike now flowing through).
- **Digital monetization** — years away from being 10–20% of revenue.
management quality / tone: - Confident, candid, numbers-fluent (Girish handled almost all Q&A). Honest about circulation drift ("we lose some copy, we gain some copy… teams go through frustration") and refusal to give guidance. Deliberately guarded on digital team size (competitive confidentiality).
non-obvious takeaways:
- Print ad growth is an outlier vs broadcasters' soft 1Q — supports the "print resilient in leadership Hindi/Gujarati markets" thesis.
- DAVP (government) +26% rate hike is a quiet tailwind driving double-digit government ad growth.
- Cover price frozen by choice (INR 4.93) — ad growth lets them subsidize readers to defend copies/market share; realization lever intentionally unused.
- Newsprint QoQ (+8%) already at ~INR 53,000; Q2 pain, then H2 relief is the key margin swing factor to verify.
